summary: Reserves an Enterprise Number, in the SMI Network Management Private Enterprise Code space, for use in documentation. Writers can then use this number in examples without borrowing a real company's number. It is informational.

eli5.summary: When writing a textbook example you use a made-up phone number so no real person gets calls. This is the made-up number for network management examples.

subtitle: A reserved enterprise number, 32473, for use in examples so nobody borrows a real company's number.

tldr.problem: Examples in RFCs and books that need an Enterprise Number had no safe value to use, risking conflict and confusion with a real organization.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC sets aside Enterprise Number 32473 for use in examples in RFCs, books, documentation, and the like.
tldr.outcome: Writers can use 32473 in examples; it is not intended to be implemented or treated specially by any implementation.

today: RFC 5612 is an Informational RFC published in August 2009. No later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Enterprise Numbers
sections.content:
RFC 1065 created a subtree of object identifiers (OIDs) for management objects defined by a single party, such as an enterprise. The subtree for an enterprise is the prefix 1.3.6.1.4.1. followed by the Enterprise Number assigned to it. IANA allocates these numbers.

The numbers are also used in other protocols, for example STRUCTURED-DATA identifiers in Syslog, vendor-specific RADIUS attributes, vendor options in DHCPv4, and enterprise-specific information elements in IPFIX. Documents about these protocols may contain examples that include an Enterprise Number.
sections.eli5: Every company gets its own number, like a house number on a street, so its network settings do not mix with anyone else's.

sections.title: The Documentation Number
sections.content:
To reduce the likelihood of conflict and confusion, the RFC allocates Enterprise Number 32473 for use in examples in RFCs, books, documentation, and the like.

This number is not intended to be implemented. No implementation is expected to send it or to treat it specially when receiving it.
sections.eli5: The number 32473 is the pretend house number you put in examples. Real programs never need to use it.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content: IANA has updated the registration for Enterprise Number 32473 to point to this RFC. The RFC says the allocation has no direct impact on security.
sections.eli5: The number list now says 32473 is the pretend one, and using it does not make anything less safe.
